 Vajiram & Ravi provides Daily UPSC Prelims Current Affairs for 19 November 2026, tailored for aspirants. We cover all relevant news and events crucial for the exam, ensuring you stay updated & well-prepared.
 Barak Point Defence Missile System 
 November 19, 2026 
 Barak Point Defence Missile System Latest News 
 The Ministry of Defence recently signed a contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of Barak Point Defence Missile System onboard Indian Navy ships at an overall cost of Rs 1,976.40 crore. 
 About Barak Point Defence Missile System 
 It is a shipborne surface to air missile system built for point defence.   
 Point defence is the last layer of a warship's air defence .  
 It is meant to destroy threats that get close to the ship, such as anti-ship missiles, aircraft and drones.  
 The system was developed in Israel by Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) along with Rafael Advanced Defense Systems.  
 The original Barak point-defence system is generally identified as Barak-1.  
 The Indian Navy acquired it in 2000, and it has since been fitted on several frontline warships. 
 It is fitted on several major platforms, including the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya, Delhi-class destroyers, and Shivalik- and Brahmaputra-class frigates.  
 The Barak-1 is slated eventually to give way to the Vertical Launch Short Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VL-SRSAM), being developed indigenously by the Defence Research and Development Organisation ( DRDO ).   
 Barak Point Defence Missile System Features 
 Weight: 98 kg 
 Warhead: 22 kg  
 Length: 2175 mm 
 Diameter: 170 mm 
 Wing span: 685 mm 
 Range: 10 km 
 Velocity: In excess of Mach 2  
 It is fully automated with the fire control system capable of calculating the level of threats, allocating missile(s) and launching them automatically upon acquisition of the target(s) by the ship's radar.  
 How does Barak-8 differ from Barak-1? 
 Barak-8 is a modern medium-range air defence system jointly developed by India and Israel. 
 It is designed to defend against any type of airborne threat including aircraft, helicopters, anti-ship missiles, UAVs, ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and combat jets. 
 Barak-8 Features: 
 It has a length of about 4.5 m, a diameter of 0.225 m at missile body, and 0.54 m at the booster stage, a wingspan of 0.94 m and weighs 275 kg including a 60-kg warhead. 
 The missile has a maximum speed of Mach 2 with a maximum operational range of 70 km , which was later increased to 100 km.  
 Barak-8 features a dual pulse rocket motor as well as thrust vector control (TVC), and possesses high degrees of manoeuvrability at target interception range.  
 A second motor is fired during the terminal phase, at which stage the active radar seeker is activated to home in on to the enemy track.  
 When coupled with a modern air defence system and multi-function surveillance track and guidance radars, Barak-8 is capable of simultaneously engaging multiple targets during saturation attacks.  
 News: PIB 
 Barak Point Defence Missile System FAQs
 Q1: What is the Barak Point Defence Missile System?
 Ans: It is a shipborne surface-to-air missile system designed for point defence of naval warships.
 Q2: Which country developed the Barak Point Defence Missile System?
 Ans: Israel.
 Q3: What is the original Barak Point Defence Missile System generally known as?
 Ans: Barak-1.
 Q4: What is the operational range of the Barak Point Defence Missile System?
 Ans: Approximately 10 km.
 Surveillance Pricing 
 November 19, 2026 
 Surveillance Pricing Latest News 
 The New York City Council recently passed a bill to ban surveillance pricing, a practice in which businesses use personal data to determine what consumers pay. 
 About Surveillance Pricing 
 It is the practice of collecting personal information about consumers and charging different prices to individual (or groups of) consumers for the same goods or services.  
 Businesses can use algorithms to analyse information about an individual and estimate how much they might be willing to pay.   
 This can result in consumers shopping for the same exact product paying vastly different prices.  
 It often involves the use of data analytics, artificial intelligence , and machine learning algorithms to personalize prices based on a variety of factors. 
 These factors may include their location, income, browsing history, previous purchases, demographic characteristics, and online shopping behaviour.  
 Key Features: 
 Data-Driven: Relies on extensive data collection —clicks, time spent on page, demographics, etc. 
 Dynamic: Prices can change frequently, even minute-to-minute, based on live signals. 
 Personalized : Different users may see different prices for the same product or service. 
 Algorithmic: Driven by machine learning models that continuously learn from new data 
 Surveillance pricing is different from dynamic pricing: while airlines and ride-hailing platforms commonly adjust prices in response to demand , availability, and other market conditions, surveillance pricing relies on customer-specific information to determine what they are charged.  
 Example: 
 E-commerce: A customer in a wealthier zip code might see higher prices than one in a lower-income area. 
 Surveillance pricing is only possible if the merchant has your data. This is gathered via multiple channels, including: 
 Cookies and d evice and browser fingerprinting 
 Mobile apps that access location or device data 
 Loyalty cards and programs that log your past purchases 
 Social media activity 
 Search behavior (especially when you’re logged into accounts).  
 For example, if you sign in to Amazon and browse a particular product multiple times without buying, Amazon might infer high interest and raise the price slightly the next time you look for it. 
 News: IE 
 Surveillance Pricing FAQs
 Q1: What is surveillance pricing?
 Ans: It is the practice of collecting personal information about consumers and charging different prices to individuals or groups for the same goods or services.
 Q2: How do businesses determine the prices charged under surveillance pricing?
 Ans: They use algorithms to analyse personal information and estimate how much an individual consumer may be willing to pay
 Q3: Which factors may influence prices under surveillance pricing?
 Ans: Location, income, browsing history, previous purchases, demographic characteristics and online shopping behaviour.
 Q4: What are the different sources through which businesses collect consumer data for surveillance pricing?
 Ans: Cookies, device and browser fingerprinting, mobile applications, loyalty programmes, social media activity and search behaviour.
 Traditional Knowledge Digital Library 
 November 19, 2026 
 Traditional Knowledge Digital Library Latest News 
 The Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) Division and the CSIR–Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), people's rights over traditional knowledge. 
 About Traditional Knowledge Digital Library 
 It is a unique initiative, established in 2001 by the Government of India through collaboration between CSIR and the Ministry of AYUSH. 
 Objective: Its primary objective is to prevent the erroneous grant of patents on Indian traditional knowledge and to safeguard the country’s knowledge heritage from misappropriation. 
 Features of Traditional Knowledge Digital Library 
 It currently contains information on over 5.2 lakh formulations and practices drawn from Indian systems of medicine such as Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa Rigpa , as well as Yoga, sourced from authoritative traditional texts. 
 Under this, knowledge from multiple languages and disciplines is translated, structured and linked with modern scientific and technical terminology. 
 Languages: The database is available in five international languages— English, German, French, Japanese and Spanish. 
 To this platform, access is provided to patent offices through Non-Disclosure Agreements. 
 The TKDL is widely regarded as a global benchmark for the defensive protection of traditional knowledge. 
 Sourc e: PIB 
 Traditional Knowledge Digital Library FAQs
 Q1: What is Traditional Knowledge Digital Library ?
 Ans: It is a unique initiative, established in 2001 by the Government of India through collaboration between CSIR and the Ministry of AYUSH.
 Q2: What is the objective of Traditional Knowledge Digital Library ?
 Ans: Its primary objective is to prevent the erroneous grant of patents on Indian traditional knowledge and to safeguard the country’s knowledge heritage from misappropriation.
 CancerSpot 
 November 19, 2026 
 CancerSpot Latest News 
 The blood test, CancerSpot, that looks for cancer-related changes in DNA has shown the potential to detect multiple types of cancer. 
 About CancerSpot 
 It is a blood test that looks for cancer-related changes in DNA. 
 It was developed by Bengaluru-based Strand Life Sciences. 
 How Does the Test Work? 
 Cells in the body release small fragments of DNA into the bloodstream. These are known as circulating or cell-free DNA.  
 In people with cancer , some of these fragments originate from tumour cells and carry changes that can help identify the disease.  
 CancerSpot combines DNA sequencing with AI-based analysis to examine patterns of DNA methylation.  
 Methylation refers to chemical modifications of DNA that influence how genes function.  
 These patterns differ between cancer cells and normal cells and can be used to identify cancer-associated signals in a blood sample.  
 By analysing these patterns , the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test , without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection. 
 Recent Study: 
 It examined how DNA released by different cells in the body influences the detection of cancer.  
 An important finding was that higher levels of circulating DNA were associated with stronger cancer-related signals and better detection sensitivity , even among patients at the same stage of cancer.  
 Researchers had expected that the increased release of DNA from immune cells in cancer patients would dilute the tumour-derived DNA signals, making cancer detection more difficult. However, the study found the opposite.  
 The findings suggest that DNA released by tumour cells and immune cells increases together in cancer patients , helping strengthen the cancer-related signals in the blood. 
 This provides new insights into the interaction between tumours and the immune system and its role in blood-based cancer detection. 
 News: TH 
 CancerSpot FAQs
 Q1: What is CancerSpot?
 Ans: It is a blood-based test that looks for cancer-related changes in DNA.
 Q2: Which company developed CancerSpot?
 Ans: Bengaluru-based Strand Life Sciences.
 Q3: What is the primary objective of CancerSpot?
 Ans: To detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test.
 Q4: Which patterns in DNA does CancerSpot examine to identify cancer-associated signals?
 Ans: DNA methylation patterns which are chemical modifications of DNA that influence how genes function..
 Kerch Strait 
 November 19, 2026 
 Kerch Strait Latest News 
 Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed the road section of the Crimean Bridge across Kerch strait linking the annexed peninsula to Russia. 
 About Kerch Strait 
 Located in southeastern Europe, it is the only water body that connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov .  
 It separates the Kerch Peninsula of Crimea in the west from the Taman Peninsula of Russia in the east.  
 The city of Kerch , a port and historical site,  lies near the middle of the strait, on the Crimean side. 
 Historically known as the Cimmerian Bosporus, it has been a vital maritime route for centuries.  
 It is a narrow body of water approximately 35 kilometers long, with widths ranging from 3.1 to 15 kilometers and depths up to 18 meters.  
 It serves as a crucial passage for shipping , including Russian grain and oil exports.  
 It has also been a key point of conflict between Russia and Ukraine after Moscow annexed the peninsula from Ukraine in 2014. 
 The Crimean Bridge, completed in 2018, spans the strait, linking Crimea to mainland Russia.   
 Spanning 19-km, it includes a road and rail connection. 
 News: TG 
 Kerch Strait FAQs
 Q1: Which two water bodies does the Kerch Strait connect?
 Ans: The Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.
 Q2: Which two peninsulas are separated by the Kerch Strait?
 Ans: The Kerch Peninsula of Crimea in the west and Russia's Taman Peninsula in the east.
 Q3: What was the historical name of the Kerch Strait?
 Ans: Cimmerian Bosporus.
 Q4: Why is the Kerch Strait strategically important?
 Ans: It serves as a crucial maritime shipping passage, including for Russian grain and oil exports.
 PM SVANidhi Scheme 
 November 19, 2026 
 PM SVANidhi Scheme Latest News 
 The Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, will organise the PM SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 in New Delhi. 
 About PM SVANidhi Scheme 
 The Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme was launched in June 2020. 
 It is a Central Sector Scheme supporting street vendors through affordable working capital, financial inclusion and social protection measures. 
 Implementation: It is a joint responsibility of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and the Department of Financial Services (DFS). 
 Key Features of PM SVANidhi Scheme 
 Working Capital Loan: Collateral-free loans of ₹15,000, ₹25,000, and ₹50,000 are provided in three progressive tranches with interest subsidy and credit guarantee support. 
 UPI-linked RuPay Credit Cards: Vendors successfully repaying the second tranche are eligible for UPI-linked RuPay Credit Cards with limits up to ₹30,000. 
 Digital Adoption: Cashback incentives of up to ₹1,600 are provided to street vendors for retail/wholesale digital transactions to encourage digital adoption and financial literacy. 
 SVANidhi se Samriddhi (SSS): Socio-economic profiling of beneficiaries and their families is undertaken to link them with eight selected Central welfare schemes and create a holistic social security net.   
 Capacity Building & Entrepreneurship Development : Vendors are provided with training in financial literacy, digital literacy, and food safety & hygiene in collaboration with FSSAI. 
 Sour ce: PIB 
 PM SVANidhi Scheme FAQs
 Q1: What is PM SVANidhi Scheme?
 Ans: It is a Central Sector Scheme supporting street vendors through affordable working capital, financial inclusion and social protection measures.
 Q2: Which ministry implements PM SVANidhi Scheme?
 Ans: It is a joint responsibility of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and the Department of Financial Services (DFS).
 Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre 
 November 19, 2026 
 Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre Latest News 
 The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction technologies for mapping human settlements across Indian cities.  
 About Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre   
 It is a single-window, independent, nodal agency that functions as an autonomous agency in the Department of Space (DOS).   
 It is formed following the Space sector reforms to enable and facilitate the participation of private players. 
 IN-SPACe is responsible to promote, enable, authorize and supervise various space activities of non-governmental entities (NGEs) including  
 Building launch vehicles & satellites and providing space-based services;  
 Sharing space infrastructure and premises under the control of DOS/ISRO; and  
 Establishing new space infrastructure and facilities. 
 The agency acts as an interface between ISRO and NGEs and assesses how to utilize India’s space resources better and increase space-based activities.  
 It also assesses the needs and demands of private players, including educational and research institutions, and explores ways to accommodate these requirements in consultation with ISRO . 
 Headquarters: Ahmedabad, Gujarat  
 Three Directorates viz., Promotion Directorate (PD), Technical Directorate (TD) and Program Management and Authorization Directorate (PMAD) are carrying out the functions of IN-SPACe. 
 Sou rce: IS 
 Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre FAQs
 Q1: What is Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre ?
 Ans: It is a single-window, independent, nodal agency that functions as an autonomous agency in the Department of Space (DOS). 
 Q2: Where is headquarter of Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre located?
 Ans: Ahmedabad, Gujarat 
 Palaeoloxodon Namadicus 
 November 19, 2026 
 Palaeoloxodon Namadicus Latest News 
 Researchers discovered a fossilised jaw along the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh and revealed that this 75-cm-long remains may belong to Palaeoloxodon namadicus. 
 About Palaeoloxodon Namadicus 
 It is an extinct straight-tusked elephant species that was among the largest elephants to have ever lived. 
 The species is considered one of the largest land mammals known to have existed. 
 Its remains have been found in geological deposits associated with the Pleistocene period, which lasted from around 2.6 million years ago to approximately 11,700 years ago. 
 It was found at Patai Ghat near Patai village in the Deori tehsil of Madhya Pradesh's Raisen district. 
 Distribution: It is mostly known from several post-Siwalik hills Pleistocene beds of India . 
 The type locality is in Narmada-Godavari region of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra-Telangana respectively, with additional report from Ganga valley of Uttar Pradesh and Bankura district of West Bengal. 
 Features of Palaeoloxodon Namadicus 
 It is the largest proboscidean currently known, reaching a should height of 4.5 to 5 metres and a mass of 18 to 19 tons at max, making it slightly larger than the European Straight Tusked Elephant 
 Sou rce: IE 
 Palaeoloxodon Namadicus FAQs
 Q1: What is Palaeoloxodon Namadicus ?
 Ans: It is an extinct straight-tusked elephant species that was among the largest elephants to have ever lived.
 Q2: Where was Palaeoloxodon Namadicus fossil discovered recently?
 Ans: It was found at Patai Ghat near Patai village in the Deori tehsil of Madhya Pradesh's Raisen district.
 White-Bellied Heron 
 November 19, 2026 
 White-Bellied Heron Latest News 
 Researchers from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) recorded a sighting of the critically endangered White-Bellied Heron along the Lohit River in Arunachal Pradesh recently. 
 About White-Bellied Heron 
 It is a large, fish-eating bird found across parts of the Eastern Himalayas .  
 Scientific Name: Ardea insignis  
 It is also known as the imperial heron or great white-bellied heron. 
 It is regarded as one of the world’s most threatened bird species – listed amongst the top 100 most Evolutionarily Distinct and Globally Endangered (EDGE) species. 
 White-Bellied Heron Habitat and Distribution 
 It is mainly living in the foothills of the eastern Himalayas in northeast India and Bhutan to northern Myanmar. 
 There are few records of observation from southern China.  
 In India , it occurs in the states of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.  
 It inhabits undisturbed, pristine river systems and wetland habitats in the subtropical and temperate forests of the eastern Himalayas.  
 Its global population is estimated to be extremely small, with fewer than 100 mature individuals. 
 India is believed to have fewer than 10 individuals surviving in the wild. 
 White-Bellied Heron Features 
 Standing nearly a metre tall , it is the second largest living species of heron . 
 It has a slightly longer neck and compact body with shorter legs and extensive toes. 
 Its body is dark greyish with contrasting white throat, belly, and vent, and white-streaked scapulars, foreneck and upper breast.  
 The legs and feet are dull grey.  
 The extra elongated, flexible neck with razor-sharp serrated black bill allows them to catch fish far in deep waters. 
 White-Bellied Heron Conservation Status 
 It is classified as ' Critically Endangered ' under the IUCN Red List. 
 News: MC 
 White-Bellied Heron FAQs
 Q1: What is the White-Bellied Heron?
 Ans: It is a large, fish-eating bird found across parts of the Eastern Himalayas.
 Q2: Which geographical region is the White-Bellied Heron primarily found in?
 Ans: The foothills of the Eastern Himalayas.
 Q3: Which countries are part of the distribution range of the White-Bellied Heron?
 Ans: Northeast India, Bhutan and northern Myanmar, with a few records from southern China.
 Q4: What are the distinctive physical features of the White-Bellied Heron?
 Ans: A dark greyish body, white throat, belly and vent, and white-streaked scapulars, foreneck and upper breast.
 Q5: What is the IUCN Red List conservation status of the White-Bellied Heron?
 Ans: Critically Endangered (CR).
 Climate Risk Index 2027 
 November 19, 2026 
 Climate Risk Index 2027 Latest News        
 India is the tenth most climate vulnerable country in the world over the past three decades (1996-2025), showed the Climate Risk Index 2027.  
 About Climate Risk Index 2027     
 It is a tool that assesses extreme weather events’ impacts on countries and regions. 
 Published by: Climate Risk Index has been published since 2006 by Germanwatch. 
 It analyses climate-related extreme weather events’ degree of effect on countries. 
 It is one of the longest running annual climate impact-related indices. 
 It ranks countries based on these events’ economic and human impacts one year before publication and over the preceding 30 years. 
 It examines hydrological, meteorological, and climatological events . Fatalities and economic loss from seven hazard types are included in these categories. A composite score is then generated for ranking countries. 
 Key Highlights of Climate Risk Index 2027 
 From 1996 to 2025, more than 916,000 people lost their lives worldwide due to climate-related extremes and direct economic losses exceeding USD 4.7 trillion (inflation-adjusted) were incurred. 
 Deadliest hazards: Heatwaves were by far the deadliest extreme weather events in 2025. 
 Costliest hazards: Storms are by far the costliest hazard over the three-decade period, accounting for 58% of economic losses in 1996–2025.  
 Sou rce: DTE 
 Climate Risk Index 2027 FAQs
 Q1: Which organisation publishes Climate Risk Index ?
 Ans: Germanwatch
 Q2: Climate Risk Index analyses which events?
 Ans: It analyses climate-related extreme weather events’ degree of effect on countries.
